obtained.how: the news item on the Associated General Contractors of Maine's own web site

bibliography.note: Title 'N.S. Giles Wins Specialty/Subcontractor Award for its Danforth Fishway Project', date posted April 16, 2024. Matches.

claims.claim: alewives gathered below the Danforth dam in the years before the fishway was built
claims.source_value: over the past four years (to April 2024) alewives were seen at the base of the Baskahegan Dam for the first time in two centuries
claims.location: web page, paragraph beginning 'The Danforth Fishway Project, by helping to establish a self-sustaining alewife run'
claims.quote: alewives have been spotted at the base of the Baskahegan Dam
claims.conditions: a contractors' association news item; no counts or dates
claims.note: AGC names it the Baskahegan Dam (project title 'Danforth Fishway-Baskahegan Lake and Crooked Dam').

claims.claim: a pool-and-weir fishway was built there in 2023 and dedicated in August 2024 (AGC Maine 2024; ASF 2024)
claims.source_value: a pool and weir fishway at the Baskahegan Dam, led by the Atlantic Salmon Federation, an over-$1 million project that N.S. Giles completed in four months; Hurricane Lee flooded the site two weeks after work began
claims.location: web page, first and fifth paragraphs
claims.quote: constructing a pool and weir fishway at the Baskahegan Dam
claims.note: AGC confirms the pool-and-weir fishway; it gives no year (only Hurricane Lee's arrival during construction, and a post date of April 2024) and, being earlier, nothing about the August 2024 dedication. The year 2023 and the dedication come from ASF 2024 ('constructed in 2023'; dedication Saturday, August 10).

notes: The project 'aims to reopen access to nearly 8,960 acres and 137 miles of stream habitat for alewives and other migratory fish species' (first paragraph). Owner Atlantic Salmon Federation; general contractor Sargent Corporation; engineer Acadia Civil Works.
